chapter: Johnny Griffin, Hampton and club life
title: Johnny Griffin, Joe Henderson and Griffin's drinking
summary: Segal remembers Griffin from Roosevelt, a shared birthday with Joe Henderson, and Griffin's heavy drinking.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now I also had in my notes here when I was researching this, there was one gentleman that jumped out here. It was identified as a favorite of yours... Johnny Griffin.
And Johnny, being a part of those early days with the Jazz Showcase?
Oh yeah, he’s - I have pictures of him up at Roosevelt.

After he came off the Hampton band, because he came off very early, he was just seventeen or eighteen. And Griffin was around, and then we did an album with Ira and Griffin, where they changed saxes and all. Baritone, alto, and tenor, and then Ira also played trumpet and flugelhorn. Griffin has the same birthday as me, April 24th, as did Joe Henderson, and I happened to get them both together one time at the Blackstone Hotel. Pardon me for saying it, but it was no contest.

No. Griffin just overwhelmed Joe Henderson. It was a completely different kind of playing, you know. But Griffin, I don’t know how he could play, cause he used to get pretty blasted, and when he’d come home from Europe for his birthday week he’d start out the beginning of the week at his south side home with his mother and family and friends, and they’d have a party. They’d have a party all week.
But at time he came to the club, I mean you think he couldn’t even lift the horn, cause you know, tenors are pretty heavy if you ever lift one.

And he’d play his butt off. So later on, toward the end of his stint with us we had the bar there in the club. He said, “Joe, I can’t do this anymore because the doctor told me, you know, I can’t drink.” I said, “Well, ok. We’ll close the bar down.” He says, “Well, then I’ll have to go next door and drink!” [Laughs] But he was a sweetheart.
